steps: Unpack & inspect
Unpack carefully and check the stove and every part for transit damage; confirm all parts are in the box. Report damage or missing parts to the dealer immediately.
Site the stove

Freestanding only — not in a mobile home, any factory-built fireplace or a sleeping room. No outside combustion air is required (no kit exists); check clearances to walls, floor, ceiling, cabinets, fireplace and chimney.

• Freestanding cook stove only; not for installation in any factory-built fireplace.
  • Not approved for a mobile home. Do not install in a sleeping room (p. 16).
  • No additional outside air for combustion; no kit is available.
  • Open area away from traffic flow, doors and hallways, near the chimney; never where gasoline, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or other flammable liquids are used or stored (p. 3).
  • Decide the floor (as is, or with a floor protector) and check clearances to walls, floor, ceiling, cabinets, fireplace and chimney before connecting.

Hearthstone recommends installers certified by NFI (U.S.) or W.E.T.T. (Canada) (p. 1). Check permits, restrictions and inspection with local building or fire officials.
Floor protection

Noncombustible protector, R-value 0.89 min or UL listed, extending 16" (US) / 46 cm (Canada) past the fuel loading door and 8" (20 cm) past each side. Horizontal connector: protect beneath it and 2" past each side.
Clearances & alcove
Lay out to the p. 9 table (single vs double wall, top vs rear exit; letters per Fig. 2). Alcove: 48" max depth, 96" min height, 63" / 58" min width (single / double wall connector).
Chimney connector

6" (152 mm) 24 or 25 MSG blued steel, or listed close-clearance double-wall pipe; crimped ends toward the stove, at least three #10 x 1/2" screws at the flue collar. Never through a floor, ceiling, attic or concealed space; thimble through combustible walls.

Single wall6" (152 mm), 24 MSG or 25 MSG blued steel
Double wall (close clearance)tested to UL standards and listed; e.g. Simpson Dura Vent DVL, Metalbestos DS; also acceptable: Security, GSW, Ameritec
Flue collarat least three #10 x 1/2" sheet metal screws into the pre-drilled holes

No aluminum or galvanized pipe. Crimped ends toward the stove so creosote runs back into it. Double-wall connector must be used with a listed factory-built Type HT chimney and may also be used with a masonry chimney to reduce clearances. Through a combustible wall, conform to NFPA 211 or CAN/CSA - B365 and use a wall thimble; to a prefabricated chimney, use a wall pass-through. Don't use stovepipe as a chimney or liner. Never connect to a flue serving another appliance, or to any air distribution duct or system.
Run & draft
Keep the stovepipe short and straight, horizontal runs rising at least 1/4" per foot (21mm/m) away from the stove. Draft must be 0.06" – 0.1" w.c.; above 0.1" w.c., install a stovepipe damper.
Prefabricated chimney

Type HT (2100 deg. F), listed to UL 103 or ULC S629, installed exactly per its maker with that maker's accessories. Flue 6" (152 mm) inside diameter for new installations; an existing 8" (203 mm) flue with a reducer.

Buy from the chimney manufacturer: the wall pass-through (or ceiling support package), "T" section package, fire-stops (when needed), insulation shield, roof flashing, chimney cap and any other accessories, and keep to their clearances. It can run inside (through ceiling and roof) or outside (through the wall behind the stove, then up the outside); choose an interior chimney whenever possible (p. 14). Typical layouts are shown as drawings on p. 13.

An oversized flue contributes to creosote — bigger is not better.
Rear exit: reverse the collar

Remove the flue collar's four bolts (10mm) and the rear block-off plate; mount the collar on the rear exit gasket side toward the stove, rotated for access to the 3 connector screws. Bolt the cover plate over the top exit.

1. With a 10mm wrench or socket, remove the four bolts holding the flue collar and pull it away from the stove. Check that the gasket is in place and in working order.
  2. Remove the four bolts holding the block-off plate on the back of the stove, and remove the plate.
  3. Place the flue collar over the rear flue exit, gasket side toward the stove, rotated so the 3 chimney connector screws are easiest to reach. Replace the four bolts.
  4. Place the cover plate over the top flue exit, using the same four bolts that were removed.

Use the rear-exit columns of the clearance table (p. 9).
Masonry chimney
Code-approved and lined; have a professional examine it and finish any repairs before installing. 8" x 8" (203 mm x 203 mm) tile for best results; the cleanout must close off completely.

Wallbrick or modular block at least 4" (102 mm), or rubble or stone at least 12" (305 mm)
Flue linermin 5/8" (16 mm), refractory mortar, at least 1" (25 mm) air space
Interior chimneyat least 2" (51 mm) to combustible structure; fire stops at floors/ceilings; insulation 2" (51 mm) from the chimney
Exterior chimneyat least 1" (25 mm) to combustible structure (p. 15)

An equivalent flue liner must be a listed chimney liner system meeting type HT requirements, or other approved material. An interior chimney heats faster, drafts better and builds less creosote than an exterior one.
Chimney height

13 feet (4 m) minimum, 30 feet (9 m) maximum. At least 3 feet (0.9 m) above the highest part of the roof opening it passes through, and 2 feet (0.6 m) above any part of the roof within 10 feet (3 m), measured horizontally from the chimney top.

panels.title: Stove smokes
items: Operating technique → open the primary air fully a minute before opening doors; open the flue bypass fully
Cold chimney → preheat it when first starting a fire
Blocked chimney → check chimney and stovepipe for blockage or creosote
Oversized chimney → reline; undersized → draft inducer or new chimney; too short → lengthen it
Air leaks or another appliance on the flue → seal connections and clean-out doors; disconnect other appliances

panels.title: Back-puffing
items: Operating technique → primary air fully open a minute before opening the door, and for a few minutes after reloading
Extra low burn rate → burn at a higher rate
Chimney down-draft → install a chimney cap
Excessive ash build-up → empty the ash pan more often

panels.title: Uncontrolled or short burn
items: Unsealed or open door → close it tightly or replace the gaskets
Excessive draft → check the install, run at low burn, fit a stovepipe damper (over 0.1 wc); close the flue bypass completely
Deteriorated cement seals → reseal with furnace cement
Extra long chimney → shorten it or fit a stovepipe damper
High winds or hilltop location → install a chimney cap

panels.title: Insufficient heat
items: Poor quality or green wood → air-dried wood only, preferably dried at least one year
Low burn rate → run at a higher burn rate
Air insulated chimney → replace with a pre-fabricated insulated system or a properly sized masonry chimney
Cold exterior chimney → reline or insulate it
Leaky stovepipe or chimney → check the installation; heat loss from the house → caulk windows, seal openings

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
First find the controls: the flue bypass handle at the top center, the primary air lever on the lower part of the ash door, and the fuel door handle. Lift that handle to 9 o'clock to open the door; lower it to 6 o'clock to latch it, then pull gently to check.

  1. Open the door. Put five or six double sheets of tightly twisted newspaper in the center of the firebox. Crisscross about ten pieces of kindling over it, 1/2" thick and 10" to 17" long.
  2. Open the bypass: pull the handle all the way out.
  3. Open the air fully: push the lever to the left.
  4. Light the paper. Leave the door slightly open for a moment, until the kindling catches and the draft starts to pull.
  5. Close the door and let the fire burn.
  6. Once the kindling is burning, add logs, small ones first. Otherwise keep the fuel door and ash door closed.
  7. Close the bypass: push the handle all the way in.
  8. When the fire is burning well, set the burn with the air lever: left for higher, right for lower.
Never open the fuel door with the bypass closed. Pull the bypass out first.
First fires smoke a little. The paint and oils are curing. Open a few windows; it usually fades after 10 to 20 minutes and stops once the stove is cured.

oven.title: Heating the oven and cooktop
oven.html:
The flue bypass steers the stove's heat. It's the handle at the top center of the stove, and it pulls out and pushes in.

Pulled out (open)smoke and hot gases go straight to the chimney
Pushed in (closed)gases travel around the oven, then out

Keep the bypass open while you start a fire in a cold stove, until the chimney is drawing. Then push it closed — that's the most efficient way to run the stove. With the bypass open, the oven can't reach its highest temperatures. Use the bypass to control the cooktop and oven temperature.

Pull the bypass out before you open the fuel door to add wood.

Oven not getting hot?

  • The bypass may be open. Push it in to close it.
  • The oven door may not be sealing. Check the seal and repair it if needed.

The cooktop gets very hot. Don't set anything on it that isn't meant to be there; the heat can melt or burn it, and it can drip into the firebox. Never put clothing or candles on a hot stove.

burn.title: Controlling the burn
burn.html:
The primary air lever on the lower part of the ash door sets the burn. Push it left to open it (faster, hotter); push it right to close it (slower).

  • High: load the firebox fully on hot coals or a flaming fire, air fully open. Do this once or twice a day to heat the stovepipe and chimney and keep creosote down.
  • Medium: air mid-range. This is the normal setting, and the best one if you'll leave the stove unattended.
  • Low: air closed. Not for long stretches; it can build creosote.

Reloading

Pull the bypass out first. Open the door just a crack, pause, then open it fully. Load onto a bed of hot, red coals, and run with the air fully open for 20 to 30 minutes afterward.

Signs of over-firing

Short burn times, a roaring sound in the stove or stovepipe, or a discolored stovepipe. Causes: too much draft, the wrong fuel, or operator error, such as worn gaskets or burning with the fuel door or ash door open. If you suspect it, call your dealer immediately.

Never over-fire your stove. It will damage the stove. Over-firing isn't covered. The manual says any sign of over-firing voids your warranty.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural cordwood (firewood) only, and season it: split it, stack it and let it air-dry for a year. Green wood holds a lot of moisture and burns poorly.

From most heat to least

  • High: apple, black birch, hickory, locust, white oak, black beech, mesquite
  • Medium high: white ash, beech, yellow birch, sugar maple, red oak
  • Medium low: black ash, white birch, grey birch, elm, Norway pine, pitch pine, black cherry, soft maple, tamarack
  • Low: white pine, white cedar, balsam fir, spruce, aspen, basswood, butternut, hemlock

Higher-heat woods burn longer. Softwoods burn hotter and faster; hardwoods burn longer and leave more coals.

Storing it

Stack it on skids or blocks, and cover only the top. Tarps over the sides trap moisture. Don't store wood within the stove's clearances.

Never burn coal, kiln-dried wood, painted or treated wood, solvents, plywood, driftwood, artificial or wax logs, pellets, charcoal, cardboard, colored or glossy paper, trash or garbage. Never start or liven a fire with gasoline, kerosene, lighter fluid, other liquid fuels or solid fire starters. These fuels can generate carbon monoxide, which can sap the oxygen supply or even cause an explosion. Keep all such materials away from the stove.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Empty the ashes every week, or sooner if the firebox is full. Do it when the stove is cold; if the ash pan is still warm, wear fireplace gloves.

  1. With a poker, sift the ashes through the grate into the ash pan.
  2. Turn the ash door handle to 9 o'clock and pull the door open.
  3. Slide the ash pan out carefully by its handle.
  4. Dump the ashes into a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, with nothing else in it, and put the lid back on.
  5. Push the pan all the way back in, firmly, and close the ash door by turning the handle to 6 o'clock.

You can also shovel ashes out through the fuel door. Keep the ash pan fully inserted while the stove is in use. Letting ash build up can cause back-puffing.

Ashes stay hot for days. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that burns, never on vinyl flooring. Never use wood or plastic containers, or paper or plastic bags. Keep the ashes in the closed container until every cinder is cold.

door.title: Door glass and gasket
door.html:
Cleaning the glass

Clean it only when the fire is out and the glass is cool. Use a low-alkaline commercial stove glass cleaner from your dealer and follow its instructions. For heavier deposits, lift the door off, lay it face down on a bench, let the cleaner sit a few minutes, then wipe it off with a soft cloth.

No razor blades, steel wool or abrasives. Scratches weaken the glass.

Never run the stove with broken glass. Replace it right away with the ceramic glass made for this stove (fuel loading door glass, part 3030-050). Your dealer supplies it with instructions. If you fit it yourself, wear work gloves and safety glasses.

The door seal

Every other month, with the stove cool, shut the door on a dollar bill. If it pulls out with no resistance, the seal is loose: change the gasket. Gaskets normally need replacing every two to three seasons, and your dealer has a kit with instructions.

Don't slam the door or use it to push wood in, and don't let logs rest against the glass.

cooktop.title: Caring for the cooktop
cooktop.html:
The cooktop is glass. Scratches weaken it and shorten its life.

  • Lift pots and pans; don't slide them. Check that utensils have no rough spots.
  • Make sure the cooktop is clean before you start a fire.
  • Avoid boil-overs: keep the heat as low as the job allows and use a big enough pan. Cover pans to stop spatters.
  • Don't cook on foil. It can melt onto the glass.
  • Wipe up wet spots promptly, watching for steam burns, and clean off grease regularly after cooking.

Cleaning up a spill

Remove the hot pans. Wearing an oven mitt, hold a scraper and push the spill to a cool part of the cooktop, then wipe up the excess with a paper towel. Don't use that spot again until the spill is gone. Suggested cleaners: Weiman Cooktop Cleaning Creme, Cera Care, Hopes Cooktop Cleaning Creme, Cerama Bryte.

The enamel

The outside cast iron has an enamel finish. Wipe it with a damp sponge and dry it well so it can't rust, or use a standard glass cleaner. Over time, fine crazed lines may appear under the surface. That's natural, not a flaw.

creosote.title: Creosote and chimney care
creosote.html:
Slow, cool fires give off tar and vapors that condense in the chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot and can damage the chimney or even destroy the house.

Keep it down

  • Once a day, burn for 30 minutes with the primary air fully open and the flue bypass open.
  • After each reload, run with the air fully open for 20 to 30 minutes.
  • Avoid long stretches of low burning.

Check for it

  • Every month, look over the stovepipe and chimney and tap the pipe. Hollow means it's most likely clean; solid or full means creosote, so clean it before using the stove again.
  • Check at the stove and at the chimney top, where it's coolest.
  • More than 1/4" (6 mm) built up? Have it removed. The manual recommends a certified chimney sweep; your dealer can name one.
  • Every season, have a qualified technician inspect the chimney and stove. Take the stovepipe down, clean it, and replace any rusted pieces.

During heavy use, Hearthstone suggests a technician check the system about every other month.

safety.title: Chimney fires and everyday safety
safety.html:
If you have a chimney or stovepipe fire

  1. If it's too threatening, leave and call the fire department right away. If not:
  2. Close the primary air control.
  3. Close the stovepipe damper, if you have one.
  4. Keep all the stove's doors closed.
Never throw water on the stove, stovepipe or chimney. The heat can flash it to steam and cause serious injury.

Afterward, leave the air closed and let the fire die out completely. Don't light the stove again until the stove, stovepipe and chimney have been inspected and any damage is fixed.

Every day

  • The stove is hot while it runs. Keep children, pets, clothing and furniture away; contact can burn skin.
  • Keep furniture, drapes and other things that burn at least 36" (0.92 m) away.
  • Keep the fuel door closed except when loading wood.
  • Have a smoke detector, and keep an "A B C" fire extinguisher handy.
  • Never put clothing or candles on a hot stove.

warranty.title: Warranty registration
warranty.html:
Hearthstone manufactures and warrants the stove. As the original purchaser, you can register on Hearthstone's website (hearthstonestoves.com), or mail the signed registration form from the cook stove warranty packet to:

Hearthstone Quality Home Heating Products, Inc.
Warranty Department
317 Stafford Ave
Morrisville, VT 05661

Note: p. 3 says to return the registration card within 30 days of purchase to validate your warranty; p. 26 says sending the signed registration form is not a condition of warranty coverage.

For warranty service, contact your dealer.

What the manual says voids it

Damage from over-firing isn't covered, and any sign of over-firing voids the warranty. This manual doesn't list what is covered or for how long.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
Set the stove on a noncombustible floor protector (from the dealer, or metal, glass, stone, tile, etc.).

Each side8 inches (20 cm)
Horizontal connectorbeneath the connector and 2" beyond each side
RatingR-value of at least 0.89, or UL Listed floor protection

Example: a continuous layer of listed backer board (Micore, Wonder-Board or Durock) with a tile, brick, slate or other noncombustible facing. Figure 1 shows hearth protection for top vent installations.

Checking an alternate protector

  • R-value given: use it as is.
  • K-factor with thickness T in inches: R-value = 1/K x T.
  • C-factor: R-value = 1/C.
  • Several layers: add the R-values.

If the total is greater than the specified R-value, the setup is acceptable.
